import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 146

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/146](https://www.erdosproblems.com/146)
- [ErSi84] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M., *Cube-supersaturated graphs and related problems*.
  Progress in graph theory (1984), 203-218.
- [OpenAI26] OpenAI, *Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science*. (2026).
-/

open Filter SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos146

/--
If $H$ is bipartite and is $r$-degenerate, that is, every induced subgraph of $H$ has minimum
degree $\leq r$, then
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;H) \ll n^{2-1/r}.$$

The answer is no. OpenAI [OpenAI26] give a connected bipartite `2`-degenerate `H` and constants
`c, ε > 0` with $\mathrm{ex}(n;H)\geq cn^{3/2+\epsilon}$ for all large `n`, which exceeds the
conjectured $n^{2-1/2}=n^{3/2}$. See `erdos_146.variants.two_degenerate_counterexample`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_146 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (r q : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin q)),
      0 < r → H.IsBipartite → H.IsDegenerate r →
        Asymptotics.IsBigO atTop
          (fun n : ℕ => (extremalNumber n H : ℝ))
          (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) - 1 / (r : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

/--
The counterexample: a connected bipartite `2`-degenerate `H` whose extremal number exceeds
$n^{3/2+\epsilon}$ infinitely often, so the `r = 2` case of `erdos_146` fails.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/openai/ten-proofs/blob/94bc0feb6a9ff12c7d31d6de640a725c9d43d2b6/CompactnessAndDegeneracy.lean"]
theorem erdos_146.variants.two_degenerate_counterexample :
    ∃ (q : ℕ) (H : SimpleGraph (Fin q)),
      H.Connected ∧ H.IsBipartite ∧ H.IsDegenerate 2 ∧
      ∃ c ε : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ 0 < ε ∧
        ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
          c * (n : ℝ) ^ ((3 : ℝ) / 2 + ε) ≤ (extremalNumber n H : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos146

reformulations.difference: The primary paper defines r-degeneracy using every nonempty subgraph. Lean instead tests finite vertex subsets and counts neighbors within them, thereby testing induced subgraphs. The same definition is used in the counterexample declaration.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On the finite vertex type Fin q, every vertex subset is represented by a Finset, and neighborsWithin counts exactly the degree in its induced subgraph. Any subgraph on that vertex set has no greater degree at any vertex, so the induced-subgraph condition implies the arbitrary-subgraph condition; the converse follows by choosing the induced subgraph itself. Empty vertex sets impose no extra condition. Both the induced-minimum-degree equivalence and the arbitrary-subgraph equivalence were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: OpenAI, Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science (2026), Chapter 10, especially §1.2, Theorem 1.2, Fact 6.1, and the final padding argument: https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/ten-proofs-oai.pdf
Erdős and Simonovits, Cube-supersaturated graphs and related problems (1984), pp. 203–218: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1984-04.pdf
Erdős, Some recent results on extremal problems in graph theory (1967), especially p. 120, equation (9): https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1967-22.pdf

review.notes: Both statements match the cited OpenAI paper. In particular, Theorem 1.2 gives the lower bound for all sufficiently large n, exactly as the Lean variant states; its docstring's 'infinitely often' is a weaker summary. I compiled the exact linked external proof and derived both exact repository statements in /workspace/review/certified_comparison.lean. Their axiom reports contain only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, supporting answer(False), both solved tags, and the formal_proof record. Additional Lean checks covered positive-constant big-O bounds, empty and one-vertex hosts, edgeless forbidden graphs, and small degeneracy examples. The current erdosproblems.com page was blocked by Cloudflare despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so its latest remarks/status could not be inspected directly; the mathematical statements and resolution were independently verified from the primary paper and checked proof.
